title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33050v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.

title: Some Expressions involving Bernoulli, Harmonic, and Stirling Numbers
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33073v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we establish several identities involving Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers. Our approach extends the method developed by Kargin and Mutluer.

title: Quantitative Resolvent Calculus for Sample Covariance Matrices
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33087v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we develop a quantitative resolvent calculus for sample covariance matrices tailored to applications in high-dimensional statistics. We treat single resolvents, their derivatives, and products of two resolvents with different spectral parameters in the proportional-dimensional regime. Our bounds hold uniformly over compact subsets of $\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R_{\geq0}$ with approximation errors of order $O_{\mathbb P}(\|\Theta_n\|_F/\sqrt n)$ for deterministic test matrices $\Theta_n$. These bounds require only uniformly bounded fourth moments and a uniformly bounded population covariance operator norm. Neither regular spectral edges nor convergence of the population spectral distribution is required. As a key technical ingredient, we develop an averaging argument for centered quadratic forms involving one or two leave-one-out resolvents. Applications of our results include precision-matrix shrinkage, prediction risk in ridge regression, and generalized cross-validation. For these problems, we obtain quantitative guarantees for estimation and data-driven parameter selection.

title: Packaging Systems: Intrinsic Structure, Recovery Ranks, and Globalization Theorems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33092v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We define packaged structures through carriers, internal units, incidence, candidate spaces, and selected families. A realized packaging system additionally retains a context and formation datum related to its output by a possibly partial, multivalued realization relation. We establish comparison-relative recoverability and non-collapse criteria and an intrinsic refinement-completion theory.
  For atlas specializations, exact extension becomes a specialization-relative packaging completion problem. Under additional recovery and elimination axioms, we establish general globalization sufficiency criteria and sharp classifications for three classes of compatible finite atlases on a fixed cover $\mathcal H$. A geometric obstruction rank $
u(\mathcal H)$ yields thresholds $2k+1<
u(\mathcal H)$ for empty-preserving closures of local Carath'eodory number at most $k\ge1$; $d<
u(\mathcal H)$ for complete functional-dependency theories of local minimum Armstrong size at most $d\ge3$; and $3<
u(\mathcal H)$ for transitive relations, including equivalence relations.
  For nonempty finite label sets and empty-preserving closures, minimum commutant realization dimension equals minimum Armstrong size. We also determine intrinsic recovery ranks and construct canonical clique completions under bounded conformality without chordality. Explicit obstructions establish sharpness; a transport hypothesis is essential for the general recovery--obstruction converse. Complexity bounds apply locally, not necessarily to global extensions.

title: Formalising John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica in Lean 4
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33104v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica (Antwerp, 1564) contains twenty-four numbered theorems about a single composite alchemical glyph, presented in the manner of Euclid: theorem, demonstration, corollary. In this note the following question is considered: which of Dee's theorems can be stated precisely in a proof assistant, and which of them can then be proved? Working in Lean 4 (v4.35.0) with the core library only (without Mathlib), we divide the treatise into three layers: the syntax of the glyph, encoded as inductive data; Dee's arithmetic, verified by kernel computation; and the geometry of the final theorems, in connection with which we prove a classical result not stated by Dee: no ratio of whole numbers doubles the cube, that is, the cube root of two is irrational (the Delian obstruction). The accompanying file Monas.lean compiles with no errors and no sorry. Two observations are made. The cabalistic computation of Theorem XVII, according to which the Cross, "by the best kabbalistic computation," signifies the number 252, is verified, and its proof depends on no axioms: it is a pure computation. The only theorem of the formalisation with genuine mathematical content, the Delian obstruction, is proved constructively and depends only on the axioms propext and Quot.sound.

title: Some new criteria for the uniqueness of limit cycles in Rayleigh--Lienard systems
authors: Hebai Chen, Dongmei Xiao, Rui Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33114v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for
  Rayleigh--Li\'enard systems with damping of positive
  odd degree in the velocity are established.
  Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique
  and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by
  the damping signs.
  Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping
  and restoring functions is required.
  Changes of variables and time yield further criteria
  for generalized Kukles systems.
  Applications to three polynomial families yield
  uniqueness and nonexistence results.
  In particular, we resolve an open uniqueness problem
  for a hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator
  left open by Chen et al. (Phys. D, 2021).
  We also give an alternative uniqueness proof for
  a system with homogeneous components and obtain
  uniqueness and nonexistence results for a modified
  hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator.

title: A new family of deformed trigonometric functions and their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations: application to the nonlinear harmonic oscillator
authors: P. R. Gordoa, A. Pickering, D. Puertas-Centeno, E. V. Toranzo
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33121v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work we present an extension of the classical trigonometric functions which include, amongst others, the Lindqvist p-trigonometric functions. Additionally, we show their relevance in the study of certain versions of the nonlinear harmonic oscillator equation. Furthermore, we study their more important mathematical properties and obtain their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations. We also define a new extension of the Beta and Ateb sine functions using these new $\chi$-trigonometric functions. Indeed, these new Beta and Ateb functions are involved in the closed form expressions obtained for the solutions of the nonlinear oscillator under certain constraints.

title: Flocking with finite communication speed: a Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33170v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates. For two agents in one spatial dimension, we prove asymptotic flocking for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories, assuming only that the influence function has a divergent integral at infinity. A bounded geometric correction extends this result to arbitrary spatial dimension when all values of the initial velocity histories lie on one common affine line. For multiple agents in one dimension, we obtain uniform delay bounds, and thus flocking, provided that a fixed agent is leftmost for all sufficiently large times. In all these flocking regimes, the spatial diameter remains uniformly bounded and the velocity diameter decays exponentially. We also derive a conditional criterion involving logarithmic sums when the leftmost agent changes infinitely often. Finally, we construct a multidimensional analogue of the Doppler-inspired functional and identify an additional assumption needed to obtain delay bounds in the general case.

title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
authors: Joanna Zou, Han Cheng Lie, Youssef Marzouk
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fr\'echet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fr\'echet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Lo\`eve expansion of the same truncation order.

title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33218v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.

title: Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33226v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field. We prove that a cubic or quartic Kolmogorov vector field having the unit circle invariant has no circular limit cycle, and that a quartic vector field with two concentric circular limit cycles has at most three circular limit cycles, this bound being sharp.

title: On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33228v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.

title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
authors: Silvia Bertoluzza, Gabriella Bretti, Micol Pennacchio, Christophe Prud'homme
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33260v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

title: Sharp Bounds on Continuous Treatment Effects under Unobserved Confounding
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33278v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study partial identification of conditional treatment effects with a continuous treatment under unobserved confounding. We target the conditional average potential outcome (CAPO) E[Y_x|z] and the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) between two treatment levels. We assume a bounded outcome and Lipschitz continuity of the response functions and of the propensity scores given the latent confounder, and show that these conditions imply the smooth treatment response and smooth treatment selection conditions of Kim et al. (2018). The combined bound of Kim et al. uses only two reference points on the identified diagonal and is generally loose. Bounding through every diagonal reference point instead gives explicit bounds whose average is the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment, inside or outside the observational support. Capping the difference between the upper and lower bounds gives sharp causal bounds on the CATE. These bounds are informative without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.

title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33284v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition.

title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33287v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

title: On the transformation of unbounded convergent sequences by linear operators on Banach lattices
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33289v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.

title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33302v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Blind random search is a simple global optimization method that only requires the value of the loss function, without needing gradient information or an explicit loss model. However, its classical formulation assumes that the loss evaluation is noise-free, which limits its direct application to practical problems with noisy measurements. We extend blind random search by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with the running average of noisy loss measurements. Under the stated assumptions, we prove that the proposed algorithm converges almost surely to the global minimizer. We further analyze the rate at which the loss at the current estimate approaches the minimum loss. For low-dimensional cases, we obtain an almost sure asymptotic upper bound on the difference between the two, and for high-dimensional cases, we prove that this difference, suitably scaled, has an exact Weibull limiting distribution.

title: Statistical inference for boundary constrained parameters
authors: Jaeseon Lee, Anirban Bhattacharya, Suhasini Subba Rao
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33321v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Estimation and inference under boundary constraints arises in many areas of statistics, but the available asymptotic theory remains limited and fragmented relative to the classical case, where the parameter lies in the interior of the parameter space. In this paper we derive a boundary-constrained analogue of the standard asymptotic expansion for a minimiser of a loss function, in which the deviation of the estimator from the population parameter is decomposed over lower-dimensional subspaces determined by the directional derivatives at the minimiser. Using this decomposition we show that the limiting distribution of the estimator is a mixture of point masses and truncated skew-normal distributions, with mixture probabilities determined by the directional derivative conditions. A consequence of this result is that the constrained and unconstrained coordinates do not separate: the presence of parameters on or near the boundary affects the sampling distribution of the unconstrained parameter estimators. We apply the expansion to obtain the asymptotic distribution of the quasi log-likelihood ratio statistic under a range of null hypotheses, and since the resulting mixture is not pivotal in the quasi-likelihood setting, we propose a simulation-based procedure for approximating critical values. The framework unifies and simplifies several existing results. We illustrate the methodology by testing for interactions in exponential family graphical models, where the parameters are subject to compatibility constraints that ensure a joint distribution exists.

title: The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33328v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.

title: First-order Methods for Variational Inequality Problems with Semi-Infinite Constraints
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33329v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies first-order methods for monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints and presents this model as a framework covering constrained saddle-point problems, robust optimization, distributionally robust function-constrained optimization, and generalized Nash equilibrium formulations. Since feasibility must hold over infinitely many indexed constraints, direct projection onto the full feasible region is generally difficult. Therefore, we propose a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) that updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections only onto simple sets. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing how the achievable rates depend on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block. For coupled convex-concave saddle-point problems, strong convexity in the minimization block can accelerate its smooth terms even without strong concavity in the maximization block. We also develop an adaptive smooth variant with $O(1/K)$ VI-gap and feasibility guarantees without an a priori bound on generated multipliers. Moment-based and Wasserstein distributionally robust models fit within the framework, and numerical experiments on robust quadratic instances and distributionally robust learning illustrate the method's optimality and feasibility behavior.

title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33341v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schr\"odinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x\|^p \] (where $\| \cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents $p\ge 2$, the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if $p=4$. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.

title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
authors: Giuseppina di Blasio, Giovanni Pisante, Georgios Psaradakis
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1

<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1

n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1

n$.

title: Protect the Decision, Not the Disaster: Regret-Robust Capacity Sizing and Positioning with Transportation Recourse
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33361v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An operator who positions mobile resources before a disruption faces two uncertainties that are usually treated as one: how the joint state of demand and travel conditions will vary, and which part of the resulting cost the positioning decision can actually change. Standard distributionally robust optimization (DRO) protects total cost, and therefore spends much of its protection on disruption costs that every feasible design would pay. This paper evaluates the worst-case regret of a design and compares it with the worst-case premium of total-cost DRO, and shows that the regret-to-premium ratio can be bounded before any robust model is solved: from marginals for the dependence question, and from single-scenario optima and one transport linear program for the regret question. The worst-case law is a relabelling of the operating record, reassigning every recorded period wholesale to another recorded period, except at most one, which is split. The comparator that exposes the largest worst-case regret is found by a single mixed-integer program. We derive an explicit radius where the sample-average design is exactly regret-robust. For finite scenario and design sets we compute a design's worst-case regret exactly, bound it from quantities a planner already has, and show on fleet and EMS data how law-relative regret changes capacity and positioning choices relative to sample-average and worst-cost planning. We apply the decision tree to several years of New York fleet data, including the year before Hurricane Sandy, and to two emergency-service events. The test flags the pre-Sandy year as exposed. The training-support regret bounds cover realized test regret in three of four fleet folds. On Ida, where the regret-robust allocation differed from the sample-average one, it moved units toward the boroughs the storm loaded and cost less than the sample-average design.

title: Pinching Antenna and Relay Assisted Joint Indoor Outdoor NOMA Communications with SWIPT
authors: Amit Agarwal, Susmita Sain, Keshav Singh, Sudip Biswas
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33367v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates physical layer security in waveguide-based pinching antenna systems with a mobile eavesdropper. Assuming perfect knowledge of the legitimate user's location and only statistical information about the eavesdropper's position, the ergodic secrecy rate is analyzed under Gaussian and practical finite-alphabet signaling. Since the exact ergodic secrecy rate does not admit a tractable closed-form expression, a closed-form analytical upper bound is derived using Jensen's inequality. The resulting expression serves as an efficient objective for antenna position optimization without requiring exhaustive Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results verify the tightness of the proposed upper bound and show that the optimized antenna position closely matches the optimum obtained from Monte Carlo optimization. Furthermore, practical finite-alphabet signaling is shown to exhibit secrecy-rate saturation at high SNR, identifying an effective operating SNR region. Although the antenna position is optimized using the Gaussian-based upper bound, it remains effective for practical signaling.

title: Classical cumulants from the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33382v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We realize classical cumulants and their fixed-point equations in the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra introduced by Ebrahimi-Fard and Patras, placing classical, free, Boolean, and monotone cumulants in a common algebraic framework. A concatenation perturbation of the functionals yields left and right half-shuffle equations on ordinary words without changing the coproduct or either half-coproduct. Both equations are equivalent to the classical moment--cumulant formula and uniquely determine the classical cumulants. We also obtain a Hopf-algebraic realization of the classical-to-free cumulant transform through convolution exponentiation and the left half-shuffle logarithm. A commutative diagram identifies its partition-level action with summation over non-crossing closure fibers, recovering Lehner's closure-fiber formula within the framework of the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra.

title: Robust augmented Block Preconditioning for two-phase Incompressible Inductionless MHD
authors: Bijie Song, Lingxiao Li, Jie Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33385v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we develop a robust augmented block preconditioner for three-dimensional, two-phase, incompressible inductionless MHD equations. We employ a high-order monolithic and charge-conservative arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method as base scheme, for which the solution variables are current density, velocity, electric potential and pressure. Grad-div stabilization is added in both the current density equation and discrete momentum equation. Backward Euler method is used for the time discretization. At each time step, fully coupled solution strategy is adopted. This leads to large-scale, ill-conditioned, nonsymmetric, and indefinite dual saddle-point system. To solve this system efficiently, we construct an augmented block preconditioner within the constraint preconditioning framework. The ultimate preconditioner combines the augmented Lagrangian technique with approximate block factorization for current density sub-system and fluid sub-system. The fully coupled four-field system is then solved using preconditioned FGMRES iteration. Numerical experiments confirm the high-order accuracy and discrete charge conservation of the ALE-FEM. Drop of heavy fluid in light fluid is taken as benchmark to demonstrate the robustness of the preconditioner with respect to the discontinuity of physical parameters and the mesh size.

title: Orthograph related to mutual (strong) numerical radius orthogonality on operator algebra
authors: Shaoxing Sun, Jinchuan Hou, Xiaofei Qi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33422v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal{B} (H)$ and $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{B} (H)$, respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on $\mathcal{B} (H)$ or $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.

title: Noncommutative algebraic sets are not generically nc manifolds
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33425v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A consequence of implicit function theorem is that any algebraic set is a complex manifold except at some singular points which form a strictly lower dimension algebraic subset. Accordingly, an non commutative implicit function theorem of Agler-McCarthy might suggest that a nc algebraic set is generically an nc manifold. However, in this paper, a type of nc polynomials is shown, whose zero locus has larger dimension than the nc manifold given by implicit function theorem.

title: Quantum harmonic analysis and the Differential operators on weighted Bergman spaces of bounded symmetric domains
authors: Matthew Dawson, Vishwa Dewage, Gestur Olafsson
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33428v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop quantum harmonic analysis (QHA) for operators on the parametrized Bergman space $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$ of a bounded symmetric domain $\Omega$, extending the theory previously known for the unit ball. Building on this framework, we introduce a class of differential operators acting on operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$. Combining these tools, we advance the theory of Toeplitz operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$: we establish Toeplitz approximation results via the $\alpha$-Berezin transform, construct a differential operator $D_\alpha$ that shifts the $\alpha$-Berezin transform, and obtain several characterizations of the radial Toeplitz algebra -- including one via the uniformly continuous radial operators, and one via the domain of $D_\alpha$.

title: Optimization-based Cell Average Limiters as Metric Projections: Constrained Evolution and Convergence Analysis for Convection-diffusion Equations
authors: Seungmin Lee, Sanghyun Lee, Chen Liu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33449v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The optimization-based cell average limiter enforces global conservation and bounds, and has been successfully applied to discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of a wide range of nonlinear systems, from phase-field models to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this paper, taking the heat and convection-diffusion equations as prototypes, we analyze the convergence of the scheme resulting from cell average limiting. Encoding conservation and admissibility in a differential inclusion identifies the limiter as a backward Euler proximal step in a Lie splitting of the constrained evolution. This proximal step is the metric projection onto the convex admissible set, and we prove that it is nonexpansive and stable in the $L^2$ norm, and that it does not increase the total variation of the cell averages. Combined with the standard error analysis, nonexpansiveness yields an $O(\tau+h^{k+1})$ estimate for implicit Euler time stepping with DG discretization of polynomial degree $k$ under a reverse CFL condition, together with an unconditional $O(\tau+h^{k})$ estimate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and the enforcement of the bounds.

title: Coordinate systems and maximal order complexity in Banach lattices
authors: A. Avil\'es, C. Rosendal, M. A. Taylor, P. Tradacete
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33462v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We resolve three questions arising from the study of coordinate systems and order convergence in Banach lattices. Firstly, every order (respectively, $\sigma$-order) basis $(e_n)$ for a Banach lattice $X=[e_n]$ is automatically a Schauder basis. In fact, the associated partial sum projections satisfy a maximal inequality, and hence every such basis is uniform. Secondly, we show that there is a separable Banach lattice $X$ in which the set $$ X_{\downarrow0}=\{(x_n)\in X^{\mathbb N}:x_1\geqslant x_2\geqslant\ldots\geqslant 0=\inf_nx_n\} $$ is $\mathbf{\Pi}^1_1$-complete. Finally, we construct a separable Banach lattice $Y$ for which the set $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ of increasing positive sequences which are not order bounded is $\mathbf{\Pi}^1_1$-complete. It follows that neither $X_{\downarrow0}$ nor $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ can be described in any simpler way than by the nonexistence of positive lower and upper bounds, respectively.

title: Proof of the Langberg-M\'edard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
authors: Kai Cai, Guangyue Han, Mengxi Yang, Wenan Zang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33497v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}=(V,A,S, R)$ be a directed network, where $D=(V,A)$ is a digraph, $S=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of senders, and $R=\{r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each $1\le j \le k$, there exist $k$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in $D$, one from each $s_i$ to $r_j$, then the underlying undirected network of ${\cal N}$, with unit capacities, admits a feasible $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-$(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k)$ multiflow of value $1$ for each pair $(s_i,r_i)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,k$. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and M\'edard in 2009.

title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33519v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor--repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.

title: An improved fast iterative moment method for the simulation of near-continuum gas flows with Shakhov model
authors: Zhenning Cai, Zhicheng Hu, Guanghan Li, Chunwu Wang, Xiaowen Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33537v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The fast iterative moment (FIM) method developed in [G. Li, C. Wang, and Z. Hu, Comput. Fluids, 311 (2026), 107031] achieves fast convergence for near-continuum gas flows modeled by the Boltzmann-BGK equation through alternating iterations between the high-order moment system and the consistent hydrodynamic equations. In this paper, we extend the FIM solver to the Shakhov model and improve it in the following aspects. A finite volume method with linear reconstruction is employed for high-resolution spatial discretization of both systems. Following the original FIM method, an implicit-explicit scheme treating the Shakhov collision term implicitly is adopted for the high-order moment system. A local Fourier analysis of a linearized one-dimensional BGK model reveals the need for more hydrodynamic iterations at smaller Knudsen numbers and their slower convergence on refined grids. Motivated by these findings, a Newton-multigrid method with a new regularization strategy is introduced for the hydrodynamic equations, generally providing an effective hydrodynamic correction with one step per alternating iteration, thereby reducing the need for empirical tuning. Numerical experiments for planar Couette flow, lid-driven cavity flow, and heat transfer in a bottom-heated cavity are carried out to investigate the performance of the improved FIM solver. The results demonstrate improved efficiency and robustness over the original FIM method, particularly at small Knudsen numbers, and favorable performance with both first- and second-order spatial discretizations.

title: Joint End-to-End Training of Weighted BP Decoder Ensembles
authors: Felix Krieg, Paul Bezner, Stephan ten Brink
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ensemble decoding improves decoding reliability by combining component decoders with complementary failure events. Existing approaches typically obtain this diversity from code-specific structure, such as code automorphisms, multiple parity-check representations, or targeted modifications of the message-passing graph. In this work, we instead learn the diversity of an ensemble of weighted belief propagation decoders by jointly optimizing trainable Tanner-graph edge weights. A central design question is how the training objective should distribute gradient among the ensemble members to promote complementary decoding behavior. To this end, we compare four ensemble objectives under direct gradient-based optimization and identify best-member training as the most effective approach. For a (64,32) progressive edge-growth (PEG) low-density parity-check (LDPC) code, the resulting ensemble outperforms the considered trained and untrained belief-propagation-based ensemble baselines. With 10 members, it provides a gain of approximately 0.66 dB over a single belief propagation decoder at a target frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-4}$. Similar behavior is observed for a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, indicating that the learned complementarity is not specific to PEG. Although the ensemble performance improves substantially, all trained members show a higher standalone FER. The gain therefore results from learned specialization and complementary failure events rather than uniformly improved component decoders.

title: Remarks on covariant differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s sphere
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33572v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An $SU_q(2)$-covariant first-order differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s two-sphere is constructed. The module of one-forms is explicitly given in terms of modules of sections of charge $\pm 2$ line bundles associated to the quantum Hopf fibration.

title: Ordinary algebras of complex-valued functions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A classical theorem due to Gleason, Kahane, and Zelazko states that every complex unital Banach algebra is ordinary, meaning that any linear functional mapping elements into their spectrum is a character. While Roitman and Sternfeld extended this property to algebras with bounded spectra-showing in particular that the algebra C(X) of continuous functions is ordinary when X is pseudocompact-the general case of C(X) for arbitrary topological spaces X appears to be open, as we could not locate any reference in this direction. In this paper, we show that the pseudocompactness condition is unnecessary, that is, C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X. This fact is obtained as a consequence of a more general result characterizing positive characters on a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras, which we introduce under the name of AC*-algebras. As applications, we obtain two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space X to be realcompact in terms of 1-evaluating linear functionals on C(X) and their continuity with respect to the compact-open topology. Finally, we establish a Banach--Stone type theorem showing that two realcompact spaces X and Y are homeomorphic if and only if C(X) and C(Y) are linearly isomorphic via a map that preserves invertibility.

title: A structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recently, the author refuted several conjectures about the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences. The goal of this paper is to provide a counterpart for the conjectures of Frantzikinakis--Kuca and of Leibman. The significance of this manuscript is twofold: firstly, we provide a structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions (in the sense of Frantzikinakis--Kuca), and a corresponding structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds (in the sense of Leibman). Secondly, we identify null generalized nilsequences, as a notion of smallness, which provides a structured counterpart for null sequences. In particular, in the special case of ergodic nilsystems, we answer positively a question of Frantzikinakis on the structure of multiple correlation sequences.

title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33618v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Based on mixed-norm Herz spaces, we introduce a new class of mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth and prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embedding theorems extend and improve several known results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.

title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33620v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.

title: Approximate Controllability of Neutral Integro-Differential Inclusions Associated with Hemivariational Inequalities in Banach Spaces with Uniformly Convex Dual
authors: Jyoti Jindal, Sumit Arora, Manil T. Mohan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the approximate controllability of neutral integro-differential inclusions driven by hemivariational inequalities with nonlocal inclusion conditions in a Banach space $\mathbb{V}$ whose dual $\mathbb{V}^*$ is uniformly convex, using resolvent operator theory. We first establish an equivalence between the original problem and an associated differential inclusion involving the Clarke subdifferential. Under suitable assumptions, we then prove the existence of mild solutions corresponding to admissible controls in $\mathrm{L}^2(I,\mathbb{U})$. A key contribution of this work lies in the analysis of the control construction in Banach spaces, where the duality mapping $\mathcal{J} = \partial\big(\tfrac{1}{2}\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{V}}^2\big)$ is generally nonlinear, in contrast to the Hilbert space setting, while such nonlinearity has been viewed as a technical obstruction in earlier studies. Based on this framework, we prove approximate controllability of the original system by relating it to the controllability of the associated linearized inclusion and constructing appropriate controls involving the duality mapping. Finally, we present applications to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: The closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a Z-set in the family of all bivariate Schur concave copulas, and related results
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Very recently, Problem 2.5 stated by Mesiar and Sarkoci in \cite{MeSa} and originally formulated by Durante was answered in the negative by \v{S}eliga \cite{Sel}. The author showed that the closed convex hull of all bivariate associative copulas is a proper subset of the family of all Schur concave copulas, and even computed the exact uniform distance of his counterexamples to the closed convex hull (so that the Hausdorff distance between the two families is at least $\frac32-\sqrt{2}$). Using the fact that every bivariate associative copula can be represented as a (finite or countably infinite) ordinal sum of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula $M$, and working with the Markov kernels of Archimedean copulas, we first give an alternative, simple proof of the strict inclusion. We do so by showing that convex combinations of associative copulas can assign only very little mass to \new{staircase-shaped unions of small squares covering} certain line segments parallel to the main diagonal, a result we later extend to so-called chains and staircases. Building on the first observation, we then go one step further and show that, from a topological perspective, the closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a very small subset of the Schur concave family, namely a so-called $Z$-set, and that the family of associative copulas is, in turn, a $Z$-set in its closed convex hull.

title: A new arrangement inequality (revised and extended version)
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33653v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the cyclic inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\,\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^a x_{i+1}^b\;\le\;\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{(1+a+b)/2}\Big)^2, \] where $x_1,\dots,x_n\ge 0$ and indices are taken modulo $n$. Let $N(a,b)$ be the largest $n$ for which the inequality holds for all nonnegative $x_i$. We show that $N(a,b)$ is bounded above by an explicit quantity $N^*(a,b)$ obtained from the second variation at the constant vector, and we conjecture that $N(a,b)=N^*(a,b)$. For $a=b=1$ we prove that the inequality holds if and only if $n\le 8$, which settles the case left open in the original version of this paper. For $n=4$ the inequality holds whenever $1,a,b$ are the sides of a triangle, with an explicit remainder term. We show that $N$ is monotone along rays emanating from the line $a+b=1$; this corrects and extends an earlier monotonicity statement. Finally, any $n$ nonnegative numbers can be arranged so that the inequality holds; for $n\neq 6$ this is achieved by one of $n-1$ prescribed arrangements, which yields a volume bound for every such $n$.

title: A Proof of the Langberg-M\'edard Conjecture
authors: Sirui Liu, Zongpeng Li, Baochun Li
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33655v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In communication networks, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, achieving transmission rates unattainable by routing alone in many multicast settings. In multiple unicast, where each source sends a message only to its prescribed destination, the precise capability boundary between coding and fractional routing has long remained unresolved. In this context, the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture asserts that if all sources in a directed network transmit independent messages at a common rate and every destination can recover all source messages by network coding, then replacing every arc by an undirected edge of equal capacity yields a network in which fractional routing can simultaneously deliver each source's message to its prescribed destination at the same common rate. We prove the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture for any number of source-destination pairs and arbitrary network topology. More generally, for an undirected network with a given source set and a disjoint set of allowed destinations, we establish a necessary and sufficient cut-capacity condition for simultaneous unit-rate fractional routing under every assignment of an allowed destination to each source. Networks satisfying the hypothesis of the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture necessarily satisfy this cut condition, so the conjecture follows as a direct corollary.

title: On optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent reward
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33701v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.

title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33710v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.

title: Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33717v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.

title: Learning Representative Port Subsets for Efficient Fluid Antenna Systems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33730v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) provide many candidate ports, but probing all ports for each channel realization incurs substantial online overhead. We study a complementary offline problem: compress the candidate-port space once and reuse the compressed set across future channel realizations. The method collects optimal ports from sampled training realizations, requiring only one scan of the candidate ports per realization. On a DeepMIMO 7-by-7 FAS with 49 candidate ports, 120 training realizations yield 27 representative ports on average while retaining 99.995% of the channel power gain achieved by exhaustive port selection.

title: On the power of adaption and randomization 2: Non-symmetric convex sets
authors: David Krieg, Erich Novak, Mario Ullrich
abstract:
arXiv:2610.33733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $S:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real Banach spaces, and let $F\subset X$ be nonempty, bounded and convex. We prove $$a_{2n-1}(S,F)\le 27n\min \{ e^{\rm ran}_n (S,F), e^{\rm ada}_n (S,F)\}.$$ Here $a_k$ is the minimal worst-case error of continuous affine algorithms of rank at most $k$, and $e_n^{\rm ran}$ and $e_n^{\rm ada}$ are the minimal errors of adaptive randomized and deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ continuous linear measurements. This shows that the gain of adaption and randomization, and even nonlinearity, is limited by a factor $27n$ for approximation in convex sets. We discuss the optimality of the result by examples.
